title: World Digital Library collection at the Library of Congress — rights statement and partner items (incl. Qatar National Library maps, photographs and Arabic printed books)
title_ar: مجموعة المكتبة الرقمية العالمية في مكتبة الكونغرس — بيان الحقوق ومواد الشركاء (منها خرائط وصور وكتب عربية مطبوعة من مكتبة قطر الوطنية)
topics: historic maps of Arabia and the Gulf
rights_jurisdiction: US (LoC statement); per-item PD basis recorded in register (pre-1931 publication; creators dead >70 years or anonymous >100 years)
license: Collection statement: LoC unaware of any copyright or other restrictions; materials free to use and reuse
key_findings: WDL launched April 2009 (LoC with UNESCO support); after the WDL charter ended (2020) the collection moved to loc.gov in 2021 and stays permanently accessible.

The rights page states LoC is unaware of copyright or other restrictions in the WDL collection and that the materials are free to use and reuse; it asks users to respect the cultures documented and suggests the credit form '[original source citation], World Digital Library'.

LoC lists 347 WDL items contributed by Qatar National Library (facet 'partof: qatar national library'): Gulf/Arabia maps 1478-1922, Bedford's 1862 Levant photographs, 1915-20 lantern slides (Lt. A. H. Roberts), Arabic printed books 1854-1923 incl. Bulaq Press titles.
Items are served through IIIF (tile.loc.gov image-services), so web-resolution derivatives (<=1600 px) can be requested without downloading masters.
W2-GULF-IMAGES stored 40 images from WDL items (maps, photographs, printed pages).
athar_applications: Map props for the Gulf/Red Sea 'al-Marsa' world (Muscat-Matrah 1897 plan, 18th-c. Gulf charts) and map-reasoning puzzles (how old maps distort coasts).
Authentic early Arabic print textures (title pages, library stamps, tables) for 'Dar al-Sijill' document props.
1862 albumen views of Tripoli/El-Mina for Tripoli-region settings.
limitations: The statement is the Library's assessment, not a licence; WDL items from partners may carry partner-specific expectations — Qatar Digital Library's own site asks for prior consent for commercial use of cultural materials (see ATH-SRC-2303).
1915-20 lantern slides are anonymous and possibly unpublished; under US law unpublished anonymous works are protected 120 years from creation — flagged per item (rights_review).
Catalogue descriptions are partly colonial-era (e.g., Arab Revolt context); several items were excluded by the safety filter (military, rulers, war maps).

title: Library of Congress Prints & Photographs — Arabian Peninsula photographs (Moritz 1916 portfolio of Hejaz/Jeddah/Hejaz Railway, Carpenter Collection al-Jawf views, W. H. Jackson 1894 Aden, Aden postcards)
title_ar: مكتبة الكونغرس، قسم المطبوعات والصور — صور الجزيرة العربية (محفظة موريتز 1916 عن الحجاز وجدة وسكة حديد الحجاز، صور الجوف من مجموعة كاربنتر، عدن 1894)
authors: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
rights_jurisdiction: US (item rights advisory 'No known restrictions on publication'); pre-1931 publication; Moritz d.1939 (>70 y)
license: Item-level rights advisory: 'No known restrictions on publication.'
key_findings: Only items whose JSON rights_advisory equals exactly 'No known restrictions on publication.' were stored; variants ('...on reproduction', '...in the U.S. Use elsewhere may be restricted', 'Rights status not evaluated') were skipped.

Bernhard Moritz's portfolio 'Bilder aus Palästina, Nord-Arabien und dem Sinai' (Berlin: Dietrich Riemer, 1916) gives rare pre-1930 views of Jeddah's coral-stone skyline, Yanbu, al-Ula and Hejaz Railway stations.

No PD-cleared photographs of Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, the Trucial Coast or Muscat town were found in LoC P&P for <=1930 (searches 'Kuwait', 'Bahrain/Bahrein', 'Koweit', 'Mascate', 'Qatar' returned modern or cartoon items).
W2-GULF-IMAGES stored 21 images from this set.
athar_applications: Historic Red Sea port and desert-route settings (Jeddah gate, Yanbu shore, fortified railway stations).
Oasis architecture and water infrastructure (draw-wells, mud-brick drying) as clue mechanics.
limitations: Many views are taken by European travellers/officials; captions are German/English and orientalist in tone — rewrite in an Arab, source-critical voice.
Religious sites (Mecca, Medina mosque) and military items were excluded by policy even when PD.

title: Library of Congress Prints & Photographs — Maghreb photographs and postcards (Fez, Marrakesh, Tangier, Tetouan, Salé, Tunis, Algiers, Constantine; c.1894-1930)
title_ar: مكتبة الكونغرس — صور وبطاقات بريدية من المغرب العربي (فاس، مراكش، طنجة، تطوان، سلا، تونس، الجزائر، قسنطينة)
authors: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
rights_jurisdiction: US (item rights advisory); dated <=1930 by LoC; postcard publishers (Félix, Marrakesh; Sénéro, Fez) — anonymous/corporate photography >90 years
license: Item-level rights advisory: 'No known restrictions on publication.'
key_findings: Date gate: items whose LoC 'created_published' range ends after 1930 (e.g., 'between 1900 and 1940', 'between 1920 and 1932') were skipped even when visually ideal (Rabat Oudayas, Tunis dyers' street, Tripoli-Libya postcards).
William Henry Jackson's World's Transportation Commission photographs (1894) cover Tangier, Tunis and Algiers street scenes and gates; LoC postcards cover Fez, Marrakesh and Tetouan souqs and walls.

Several LoC Maghreb albums (lot 13549 Kairouan, lot 13553 Tlemcen/Constantine) carry 'No known restrictions on publication in the U.S. Use elsewhere may be restricted' — excluded because ATHAR serves non-US markets.
W2-GULF-IMAGES stored 29 images from this set.
athar_applications: Walled-city 'al-Atlal' settings (Marrakesh ramparts, Fez gates), souq/craft witness scenes, customs-house and port gates for smuggling cases.
limitations: Postcards often name the photographer-publisher only; if a named photographer died after 1956 the EU/UK term may not have expired — flagged as residual risk.
Kairouan, Tlemcen and Chefchaouen remain thin: LoC Kairouan sets are US-only and nothing PD was found for Chefchaouen (Xauen).

title: Qatar Digital Library — Copyright & ethical terms of reuse (per-item usage terms: Public Domain, Creative Commons, Open Government Licence)
title_ar: مكتبة قطر الرقمية — شروط حقوق النشر وإعادة الاستخدام الأخلاقية
authors: Qatar Digital Library (Qatar National Library / British Library partnership)
license: Per item: Public Domain / Creative Commons / Open Government Licence (Crown copyright) / third-party permission
key_findings: QDL marks items Public Domain, Creative Commons, or (for Crown-copyright India Office material) Open Government Licence; some content is third-party material made available only with permission.

The general terms say content may not be sold, licensed or reproduced without prior written consent unless otherwise permitted, and that commercial use of cultural materials requires prior informed consent — a stricter overlay than the item licences.
Example item checked: 'Photograph No. 9 Salwa Inlet Looking S' (IOR/L/PS/12/1956, f 16; photo 9 May 1934) shows usage terms 'Open Government Licence (version 2)' with a IIIF manifest.
The QDL website and its IIIF host (iiif.qdl.qa) return HTTP 403 to this workspace's shell; per protocol no workaround was attempted, so no QDL image was stored.
athar_applications: Best long-term source for authentic Gulf administrative documents (telegrams, agency diaries, photographs of Bahrain/Kuwait/Qatar 1900-1950) — pursue via partnership or manual download by staff with per-item OGL attribution.
limitations: Item licence and site-wide terms must both be satisfied; OGL excludes personal data and third-party rights — many IOR files contain names of private individuals.
Not stored in this wave (access blocked to automated clients).

title: Open Government Licence for public sector information, v3.0 (and v2.0 as cited by QDL items) — The National Archives (UK)
title_ar: رخصة الحكومة المفتوحة للمعلومات العامة (الإصدار 3.0) — الأرشيف الوطني البريطاني
key_findings: OGL allows copying, publishing, adapting and commercial or non-commercial use worldwide, royalty-free, on condition of acknowledging the source (provider's attribution statement and a licence link where possible).

It may not be used to imply official status or endorsement; exclusions include personal data, logos/crests/Royal Arms, military insignia, third-party rights, other IP (patents, trade marks, design rights) and identity documents.
The v2.0 page cited by QDL items could not be fetched (server error); v3.0 was read and the core grant is understood to be equivalent — needs legal confirmation for v2.0 wording.
athar_applications: If QDL/IOR Gulf documents are later obtained, OGL permits use in the commercial product with attribution, excluding personal data — redact names of private persons in props.
limitations: Does not override QDL's site-wide consent requirement for commercial use of cultural materials (ATH-SRC-2303).

title: NASA Image and Video Library API and NASA media usage guidelines (US Government works; credit NASA; no endorsement; insignia protected)
title_ar: مكتبة صور وفيديو ناسا وإرشادات استخدام وسائطها
rights_jurisdiction: US (17 U.S.C. §105); outside US not formally established
license: US Government work — NASA media guidelines
key_findings: NASA states its content is generally not subject to US copyright and asks users to credit NASA; it may not be used to imply NASA endorsement; the NASA insignia/logotype is protected and may not appear with AI-generated imagery.

Some images on NASA sites are third-party copyrighted (credited to other holders); W2-GULF-IMAGES excluded items with partner credits (METI/AIST/Japan Space Systems, ESA, JAXA, universities) and removed one ISS EarthKAM item credited NASA/JPL/UCSD/JSC.
Identifiable-person rules apply to astronaut portraits; only Earth-observation frames were stored.
W2-GULF-IMAGES stored 20 Earth-observation images (Gulf, Oman, Arabia, Maghreb, Sahara).
athar_applications: 'Then and now' coast comparisons (Gemini 12 Trucial Coast 1966 vs ISS Dubai 2025) for dating/inference puzzles; night-light patterns for settlement-reasoning tasks; terrain relief maps.
limitations: Modern city skylines are not the subject (orbital scale), avoiding freedom-of-panorama issues; some ISS images were taken by non-US crew (e.g., JAXA astronauts) but are distributed as NASA images — kept only when the API lists no third-party credit.

title: Wikimedia Commons — Gulf, Arabian Peninsula and Maghreb heritage-site photographs and archive-prop files (key set verified per file: imageinfo + licence templates)
title_ar: ويكيميديا كومنز — صور مواقع تراثية في الخليج والجزيرة والمغرب العربي وملفات دعائم أرشيفية (تحقق لكل ملف)
rights_jurisdiction: per file (CC BY / CC BY-SA licences are worldwide; PD files carry PD-* templates)
license: per file: CC BY x / CC BY-SA x / CC0 / PD (template-verified); NC/ND/GFDL-only and files with Restrictions rejected
key_findings: Lesson from wave 1 applied: metadata fetched with titles=<one file> (never from generator=search), and the licence short name must agree with a Cc-by*/PD-* template on the same file page; mismatches were skipped.
The Commons API answered HTTP 429 (Retry-After 1-29 s) to most bursts from this workspace; with ~9 s spacing and Retry-After honoured, roughly half of requests succeeded, which capped Commons volume.

Modern buildings: every stored file is tagged freedom_of_panorama:low_risk (historic/heritage structure) or :review (modern building as main subject); Gulf freedom-of-panorama rules were not legally verified.
W2-GULF-IMAGES stored 22 files from this key set.
athar_applications: Present-day look of Gulf/Maghreb heritage sites (Qal'at al-Bahrain, Zubarah, Siyadi house, Jahra Red Fort, souqs) as reference for illustrators; incidental passers-by must be cropped/blurred.
limitations: CC BY-SA files fall under the wave-1 'quarantine' rule (reference/display as-is only unless legal accepts share-alike).
Uploader licence assertions are not independently verified beyond template level.

title: Library of Congress — Selections of Arabic, Persian, and Ottoman Calligraphy (African and Middle East Division, Near East Section) — item-level rights statement
title_ar: مكتبة الكونغرس — مختارات من الخط العربي والفارسي والعثماني (قسم أفريقيا والشرق الأوسط)
authors: Library of Congress, African and Middle East Division
rights_jurisdiction: Worldwide (handwritten works 16th-19th c.; creators dead >100 years)
license: Collection statement in each item record: 'in the public domain or have no known copyright restrictions and are free to use and reuse'
key_findings: The collection lists 273 items; each item JSON carries the statement that the contents are in the public domain or have no known copyright restrictions and are free to use and reuse, with the credit line 'Library of Congress, African and Middle East Division, Near East Section Persian Manuscript Collection'.
The collection HTML pages (about/rights) were not retrievable by WebFetch (client error / JS challenge); the statement was read from the item JSON records instead.

Items with religious content (Qur'an, prayers, praises of religious figures, amulets) were excluded by title filter; 15 secular items (letters, exercises, petition, ijaza, border sheets) were selected after visual preview.
W2-GULF-IMAGES stored 15 items.
athar_applications: Authentic handwriting baselines for Lab #6 (handwriting comparison): exercises (mufradat, siyah mashq) vs finished letters (insha').
Ijaza as a model for 'certificate authenticity' puzzles (approval signatures of two masters).
limitations: Many items are Persian/Indian nasta'liq rather than Arabic naskh; label script and language correctly in-product.
Text content of some items not fully catalogued — an Arabic/Persian reader should check before use (tagged).

title: BULAC (Bibliothèque universitaire des langues et civilisations) Arabic printed books and manuscripts on Internet Archive, with BiNA reuse terms (Public Domain Mark 1.0 for PD document images)
title_ar: مكتبة BULAC (باريس) — مطبوعات ومخطوطات عربية على أرشيف الإنترنت وشروط إعادة الاستخدام في مكتبتها الرقمية BiNA
authors: Bibliothèque universitaire des langues et civilisations (BULAC)
rights_jurisdiction: Worldwide (works by authors dead >70 years / anonymous pre-1900 manuscripts)
license: Public Domain Mark 1.0 (IA licenseurl; BiNA: images of PD documents under PDM 1.0, notices under Licence Ouverte/Etalab)
key_findings: BiNA's legal page states images of public-domain documents are freely reusable under the Public Domain Mark 1.0 and descriptive notices under the Etalab Open Licence with source citation, unless stated otherwise; commercial reuse is not addressed explicitly.

BULAC's Internet Archive uploads (uploader @bulac.fr) carry licenseurl Public Domain Mark 1.0 and rights 'Domaine public' per item; ~560 Arabic-language items include Maghreb lithographs (Fez) and a 19th-c. Arabic history of Constantine printed in Constantine.
W2-GULF-IMAGES stored 9 page images (Constantine print, Fez lithograph ToC, bilingual proverbs manuscript, 1781 grammar notebook, Sirat 'Antar print).
athar_applications: Maghrebi script and lithograph textures (Fez) for North-African document props; bilingual proverb manuscript for a cipher/translation puzzle.
limitations: PDM is a label, not a licence; PD status per item was checked via author death dates/item dates.
Many BULAC items are religious texts — excluded.

title: Pre-1931 illustrated books on the Gulf and Arabia digitised by the Internet Archive (key set): S. M. Zwemer, Arabia: the Cradle of Islam (1900); J. T. & M. Bent, Southern Arabia (1900); G. F. Kunz & C. H. Stevenson, The Book of the Pearl (1908)
title_ar: كتب مصوّرة عن الخليج والجزيرة قبل 1931 على أرشيف الإنترنت: زويمر (1900)، بنت (1900)، كونز (1908)
publisher: Internet Archive (scans of LoC / University of Toronto / other copies)
rights_jurisdiction: US (published 1900-1908); UK/EU & Arab states: authors died 1897-1952 (Zwemer d.1952 -> life+70 expired 2023); Kunz co-author Stevenson death date unknown (flagged)
license: Public domain (IA possible-copyright-status: NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT / 'The Library of Congress is unaware of any copyright restrictions for this item')
key_findings: These books contain rare published photographs of Bahrain (Manama village, harbour boat, a Rifa'a house interior), Muscat harbour and Gulf pearling (cargo boat, divers' huts, divers at work) — filling the 'no historic Gulf photographs' gap left by LoC.
Plate leaves were located via the IA page-number JSON and the OCR 'List of illustrations'; two plates printed sideways were rotated in the derivative (noted in tags).
Zwemer's book is a missionary publication with proselytising text and captions; only neutral plates (harbour, village, boat, compass rose, castle) were taken.
W2-GULF-IMAGES stored 12 plates.
athar_applications: Authentic pre-oil Gulf port imagery for 'al-Marsa' art direction; pearling economy (boats, divers, merchants' pearls) as a non-violent case backdrop (valuation fraud, missing pearl).
limitations: Photographs taken by Western travellers/missionaries; rewrite captions in an Arab voice and avoid their framing.
Working divers appear partially clothed (documentary labour photograph) — crop to boat/rigging for younger bands.
